subject: ventures/quick-pick-survey
professional: a survey methodologist / psychometrician who builds pairwise-comparison (Bradley-Terry / Thurstone / conjoint) preference studies, with a rating-systems statistician as second reader: first checks are that the rating update and the pooled interval match the published formulas, that a model built for time-varying skill is defensible for static preferences, and that the intervals reported to a client are honest

evidence.correctness: `npm ci` then ran the TypeScript modules directly with `npx tsx` and compared with independent Python (stdlib math, numpy, scipy 1.17.1; scripts in the session scratchpad: g.py, d.py, t1.ts, t2.ts). (1) Glicko-2 updateGlicko (src/lib/glicko2.ts) vs my own from-scratch Glicko-2 written from Glickman's paper: three single-game cases (1500/350 win vs 1500/350 -> 1662.3109 / 290.3190 / 0.0599997; 1600/100 loss vs 1400/200 -> 1565.9739 / 98.2335; 1450/120 draw vs 1550/80 -> 1459.9897 / 114.7489) agree to 1e-9 on rating and RD. My implementation also reproduces the paper's worked example exactly (1464.05 / 151.52 / 0.05999), so the reference is sound. (2) DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pool() (src/lib/groupRanking.ts) on 4 respondents (1550/60, 1500/80, 1650/90, 1400/70): TS rating 1518.40818, se 49.15985, tau 64.79806 vs Python by hand 1518.40817, 49.15985, 64.79806. (3) Davidson tie-extended Bradley-Terry fitConjointModel (src/lib/conjoint.ts) on 300 simulated trials (numpy seed 7, true beta [0.9,-0.5], nu 0.6) vs scipy BFGS maximising the same ridge-penalised likelihood: params 0.866889 / -0.420169 and nu 0.488192 agree to 6 digits, and the finite-difference Wald SEs 0.16560 / 0.14758 match my numerical Hessian inverse (0.165598 / 0.147580). The Davidson probability form e^d/(e^d+1+nu e^(d/2)) matches the textbook form with pi_i=e^u_i. Not recomputed: question selection (pairing.ts, 540 lines, randomised), the Postgres-backed routes (no Postgres server in this sandbox: only the psql client exists), the rendered pages.
evidence.completeness: Checked claims in README, site/index.html, llms.txt and docs: Glicko-2 per-respondent ratings (src/lib/glicko2.ts, ADR 0001); Davidson/BT fit (conjoint.ts, financialProfiles.ts non-dominated pairs, test passes); three perspectives (perspective.test.ts, ADR 0006); admin survey builder, pooled ranking with best/worst rank range and CSV (surveyBuilder.ts, groupRanking.ts, route files under src/app/api/admin/surveys, all present and unit-tested); couple compare routes; results report page and sample (site/results-report-for-surveys.html, site/sample-results-report.html exist; scripts/build-sample-report.mjs); vs-typeform page. 'Every API route now has a test' backed by src/lib/routeInventory.test.ts, which passes. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and `npx eslint` is clean. Open items disclosed by the project itself: CI has never run on a runner (README), page components thinly tested, no hosted instance, no outside user (site page 'Status'). I could not run the integration suite (needs Postgres), `next build`, or load a page in a browser, so end-to-end behaviour of routes against a database is taken from the repo's own record, not seen. No TODO stubs found in the files read.
evidence.verification: Ran `npm test` (vitest run, unit + simulations): did not finish in about 9 minutes in this sandbox (the simulation suites are heavy), so I stopped it and ran `npx vitest run --config vitest.fast.config.ts` (everything except *.simulation.test.ts and *.integration.test.ts): 35 files, 304 tests, all pass, 17 s. Integration suite not run (no Postgres server). Seeded three one-line mutations in core math, each run against the fast suite and reverted with `git checkout` (git status clean for the venture afterwards): (a) src/lib/glicko2.ts newMu update multiplied by 0.9 (a 10% under-update of every rating): 304/304 pass, NOT caught; (b) src/lib/groupRanking.ts DerSimonian-Laird `(q - (k - 1)) / c` changed to `(q - k) / c` (wrong between-respondent variance, so every interval is wrong): 304/304 pass, NOT caught; (c) src/lib/conjoint.ts Davidson tie term `dc / 2` changed to `dc / 3` (the model is no longer Davidson): 304/304 pass, NOT caught. Cause: src/lib/glicko2.test.ts 'reproduces the published rating and RD' only asserts 1400 < rating < 1500 and rd fell, never the published 1464.06 / 151.52 that the title names; no test pins the pooled se/tau to a hand-computed value; the Davidson tests do not check probabilities against the closed form. The heavy simulation suites might catch (a), but I did not complete them, so that is unknown. There is a large, thoughtful suite (route inventory, contrast audit, simulations that drive the real selector, ADR 0004/0008 on DB tests), so this is a pinned-values gap rather than a thin suite.
evidence.craft: Read in full: src/lib/glicko2.ts, groupRanking.ts, conjoint.ts (first 180 lines plus export list), and skimmed pairing.ts, vitest configs, package.json, vercel config. Good: Glicko-2 follows the paper step for step with a documented single-game simplification; Davidson likelihood is computed in log space with clamping; convergence tolerance is per-row with the reason written down; ridge prior documented; CSV export neutralises spreadsheet formula injection (FORMULA_LEAD in groupRanking.ts); typecheck and lint clean. Defects: invertMatrix silently nudges a singular pivot by 1e-8 instead of reporting it, so a degenerate Hessian yields huge or arbitrary standard errors without a flag (conjoint.ts:~165); MIN_RD=30 floor is applied to the stored state and then fed back as phi on the next update, a departure from Glicko-2 that is only partly disclosed; numeric (finite-difference) gradient and Hessian where analytic ones are easy for a logit model, slow and noisy at FD_STEP 1e-4; package is named survey-site and the repo carries 814-line IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md and unmerged-PR backlog docs, a lot of process text for a prototype; npm test takes more than 9 minutes here, which makes it a poor local gate (the README tells people to use `npm run verify`).
evidence.claims: Checked: README/site/llms.txt 'Glicko-2, the system chess.com's ratings are built on' (README.md:109, src/lib/glicko2.ts:3): from my own knowledge chess.com uses the original Glicko and Lichess uses Glicko-2; no file in the repo backs the statement and I did not verify it online, so treat as a probable factual error repeated on a user-facing doc. Test name 'reproduces the published rating and RD' does not (see verification). Page and README 'randomises which option lands on top so screen position cannot bias the result' is an overstatement: randomisation removes systematic position bias in expectation, it does not make position bias impossible, and no test measures it. llms.txt links the old duncan-haywood.github.io host as the live page although CLAUDE.md says that host only redirects now, and has two 'Pages' headings. 'Every ranking comes with a real confidence interval': the CI comes from Glicko RD, which is a model-based deviation with a 30 floor and a stationary-volatility assumption, not a sampling interval, though the pooled admin interval is properly random-effects (verified). Backed and honest: Disclaimer and no-warranty text on README and site page; 'Prototype ... No outside user has run a real survey ... nothing here is a measured result' (site/index.html, VENTURE.yaml stage prototype, production null); CI 'has never actually run' (README, candid); 'items whose intervals overlap share a range' is exactly what groupRanking.ts does (above/below counts use low > high); Vercel deploy button, ADMIN_KEY/ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET and the data-collection doc exist.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through (logic and docs, not a browser): a team lead wants to rank 20 options from 10 colleagues. The path is self-host on Vercel with Postgres and two secrets, paste options to POST /api/admin/surveys (an authenticated API call; the SurveyBuilder component exists and has a test), share /s/<slug>, read the pooled ranking with intervals and rank ranges, export CSV. The design is sound for that job and the honesty about ties is a real strength. Limits: the project's own docs/CONVERGENCE.md says about 5N answers are needed before a list of N items is usable and that each respondent answers a limited number, and coverage() in groupRanking.ts tells admins when too many options are thin, so a 20-item survey needs roughly 100 answers in total across the panel. No hosted demo, so a non-technical user cannot try it; setup requires a Vercel account, database and generated secrets; I could not run the stack here, and nobody outside the author has used it. The couples feature, and a bespoke deployed 'financial' survey, are product extras whose usefulness is unmeasured.
evidence.domain: Compared against Bradley-Terry / Thurstone / Davidson paired-comparison practice and Glickman's Glicko-2 paper. The conjoint branch (Davidson tie model with ridge prior and Wald SEs) is a standard, correctly implemented choice and the pooled admin interval (DerSimonian-Laird random effects over respondents) is what a meta-analyst would use; both verified numerically. Departures a methodologist would raise: (1) Glicko-2 is a time-varying skill model whose volatility and rating-period logic are designed for players whose strength changes; for a respondent's static preferences a fixed-parameter Bradley-Terry / Thurstone fit by maximum likelihood is the usual choice, and sequential Glicko updates make the result depend on answer order (the test file itself says sequential application only 'lands close to' the published value); the repo's ADR 0002 'two preference models' was not read in depth in this audit so I do not know if it argues this; (2) adaptive pair selection with random draws makes the data non-ignorable for a naive fit, partly addressed by simulation docs; (3) no respondent-quality or intransitivity check beyond an 'answer agreement' signal, no sample-size/precision planning tool beyond the 5N rule of thumb; (4) disclaimers correctly refuse hiring or medical use. A practitioner would accept the pooled output with its intervals, and would want the individual-level rating justified.

defects.what: Core statistical code is not pinned by tests: three seeded one-line mutations (Glicko-2 rating update scaled by 0.9, DerSimonian-Laird tau^2 numerator changed to q-k, Davidson tie exponent d/2 changed to d/3) all passed the 304-test fast suite. A regression in the rating math, the pooled interval or the tie model would ship silently.

Test 'reproduces the published rating and RD' asserts only 1400 < rating < 1500 and that rd decreased; the published value (1464.06 / 151.52) is never checked, so the test name claims verification it does not perform. A three-line fix would be a one-period or single-game fixture to 1e-6 (the values in this audit agree with an independent implementation).

README, glicko2.ts header and site copy say Glicko-2 is 'the system chess.com's ratings are built on'. To my knowledge chess.com uses the original Glicko, Lichess uses Glicko-2; no file backs the claim. A user-facing factual claim that is probably wrong.

Glicko-2 (a time-varying skill model with order-dependent sequential updates and a volatility term) is used for each respondent's static preferences; a fixed-parameter Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood fit (which the repo already has in conjoint.ts) is the standard choice and has no answer-order dependence. The reported 'confidence interval' is the Glicko RD with a 30 floor, not a sampling interval.
'so screen position cannot bias the result' overstates what randomising the top slot achieves, and no test measures position bias.
llms.txt points at the old duncan-haywood.github.io live-page host (now only redirects per CLAUDE.md) instead of marisstella.app, and has a duplicated 'Pages' heading.

invertMatrix nudges a near-singular pivot by 1e-8 instead of surfacing it, so a degenerate Hessian gives arbitrary standard errors with no flag; MIN_RD floor is fed back into later updates, a departure from Glicko-2.

`npm test` (unit plus simulations) did not finish within about 9 minutes in this sandbox, and the integration suite could not be run without a Postgres server, so the full gate was not reproduced; CI has never run on a runner (README).

verdict: A carefully documented, honest prototype whose maths is right: three independent recomputations (Glicko-2 single-game updates against my own implementation that also reproduces Glickman's paper example, the DerSimonian-Laird pooled rating/se/tau, and Davidson-BT parameters and Wald SEs against scipy) all agree to 6 or more digits, typecheck and lint are clean, and the 304-test fast suite passes. It does not meet the bar because verification and claims are below 3: three hand-seeded mutations in exactly that core maths all survived the suite, one test is named for a published value it does not check, and a user-facing claim (chess.com uses Glicko-2) is probably wrong and unbacked. A methodologist would also question using a time-varying skill model for static preferences, and the product still has no hosted demo and no outside user (the site says so itself). The integration suite, simulations suite, next build and pages were not run here; scores reflect only what was run. Finished (completeness 3) but not at the bar; the cheapest fixes are to pin the three computed values above in unit tests.
